description: The projected commitment is what the per-operation leaf key signs and what the verifier re-verifies. Its signing bytes are canonical insertion-ordered JSON (NOT RFC 8785 JCS — keys are NOT sorted; field order is the struct declaration order). This vector pins those bytes and their digest so any implementation reproduces the exact message the ML-DSA signature covers.
canonicalization: insertion-ordered JSON (serde_json::to_vec over the struct in declared field order); keys are NOT alphabetically sorted
two_canonicalizations_note: IMPORTANT: there are TWO distinct canonicalizations in this profile. (1) The projected-commitment SIGNING BYTES (pinned here) are insertion-ordered (NOT JCS) because an ML-DSA signature covers them and must be byte-stable in declaration order. (2) The whole-evidence DIGEST bound into the IndependenceProofV1 uses RFC 8785 JCS (sorted keys) instead — it is not signed in declaration order, only needs to be deterministic and identical across languages; the deeply-nested evidence would otherwise diverge between Rust serde_json and TS JSON.stringify. Do not apply JCS to the signing bytes or insertion-order to the evidence digest. The golden-e2e.json fixture validates the JCS evidence digest end-to-end.
signing_bytes_note: Observe the key order: commitment_version first, NOT authorization_pseudonym — this is insertion order, not JCS. An implementation that sorts keys (JCS) will produce different bytes and the signature will not verify.
hedged_signature_note: ML-DSA-65 detached_sign (pqcrypto) is HEDGED/randomized: the signature bytes differ across runs even for the same message and key. Therefore the conformance contract pins the SIGNING BYTES and their digest (deterministic), NOT a fixed signature value. A conformant verifier checks that the disclosed signature verifies against these bytes and the disclosed leaf key — it never compares the signature to a golden value.
must_hold: signing bytes are insertion-ordered (commitment_version appears before authorization_pseudonym)
the digest is SHA3-256 of the signing bytes
the holder signature verifies against these bytes and the disclosed leaf key (signature value itself is not pinned — it is hedged)
